scores.evidence: The Hybrid Link is private but not encrypted by itself, so TLS on SQL connections is required.
scores.rationale: Distributed AG mechanics (async-to-sync before planned failover, backup-restore seeding, version compatibility blocking fail-back), MLLP/MSH-10 semantics, Azure VM UTC default, and MI-link SQL 2022 caveat are all accurate, with real limits stated honestly.

scores.evidence: "Without downtime" means: an announced interruption of 5 minutes or less in the quietest hour, no data loss
scores.rationale: Solves the actual problem, resolves the zero-downtime ambiguity explicitly with clinical sign-off (A6/T17) plus a costed path to true zero, and all exclusions are explicit and justified.

scores.evidence: Background services (HL7 sender, reminder export, batch letters) run in exactly one pool.
scores.rationale: Single-writer and single-runner principles are honored consistently across flows, cutover, pilot, rollback and schema-freeze rules; component ownership and data ownership are explicit with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: run draft Invoke-Cutover.ps1 and Invoke-Failback.ps1 3 times each, and watch how the app reconnects
scores.rationale: The riskiest assumptions (failover pause, fail-back, WAN latency, hidden dependencies) are spiked in M1 before commitment, with measurable exit criteria, 'changes the plan if' clauses, and production validation via synthetic monitoring and quarterly restore tests.

scores.evidence: Every fact below about the current system is an assumption, marked with [A#] and listed in Section 5.
scores.rationale: All load-bearing assumptions are explicit with impact-if-wrong and a validation task/date, defaults are given for open questions, and estimates are consistently labeled rough.

scores.evidence: the on-prem sender sends a message but dies before marking it sent... The EHR receives two SIU^S12 messages
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures — duplicate/lost HL7, split-brain, double-booking, time-zone shift, WAN loss, ransomware, audit tampering — each with concrete detection, containment and rehearsed recovery.

scores.evidence: Run by the existing IT ops team with no new 24/7 rota... each links to a runbook in runbooks/
scores.rationale: Ownership, symptom-based alerts tied to runbooks, deployment via existing packaging plus Terraform CI, patching and incident paths are all sized to the stated 5-person team.

scores.evidence: Without Hybrid Benefit, 16 vCores of pay-as-you-go Enterprise can add roughly $10k+ a month.
scores.rationale: Identifies the dominant drivers (SQL licensing, dual-site running, ExpressRoute, log ingestion), gives labeled ranges with a validation step, concrete controls, and cost trade-offs behind D2/D6/D12-style choices.

scores.evidence: Point of no return: The on-prem replica is removed (end of M4), or any change the on-prem side can't accept
scores.rationale: Every decision carries a reversibility rating, the one-way commitments (SQL version, schema changes, replica removal) are explicitly guarded and deferred, and fail-back is rehearsed before go-live.

scores.evidence: rehost first, modernise later... Moving to PaaS during the migration doubles the number of changes in one step.
scores.rationale: The simplest design that meets the need: rehost with no rewrite, PaaS/second-region DR/second circuit explicitly deferred with triggers, and every component justified against a driver.

scores.evidence: Today: raise the T1 long-lead requests, especially the ExpressRoute order and the HIPAA risk assessment.
scores.rationale: T1–T17 have done-when criteria, dependency-ordered parallel tracks, day-one actions on the critical path, and explicit adaptation rules if spikes disappoint.

checklist.evidence: security risk assessment approved before PHI reaches the cloud... Confirm the BAA covers the services used
ADT feed from the EHR into the scheduling app, and SIU feed out to the EHR, RIS and billing
row counts and checksums on Appointment and Slot by date, max IDs, HL7 counts per hour
Only one writable database at any moment. No dual writes and no active-active setup
on-prem stays as an async secondary... Fail-back is rehearsed in M1 (T14) and in both rehearsals
ExpressRoute (primary) plus site-to-site VPN (backup)... Spike: WAN latency tolerance
Zone failure: automatic failover inside AG-AZURE, RTO under 1 minute, RPO 0... downtime-procedure runbook
2 domain controllers in the hub... PIM plus MFA... Break-glass accounts... SQL Audit sent to immutable storage
Load test at 2x measured peak... Shadow (M2): prod is replicating to the cloud, with no user traffic
5-minute pause, Sunday 02:00... Release and schema freeze starts... Hypercare runs for 2 weeks
ask the vendor for a cloud support statement... wipe and retire the hardware per hospital media-sanitisation policy

traps.evidence: The database copies itself continuously to the cloud... The move itself is one planned, lossless failover.
No dual writes and no active-active setup, because either could cause double-bookings.
Pre-production uses synthetic data only... No public IPs (enforced by policy).
HL7 traffic keeps flowing: ADT in, SIU out... channels repointed
rehost first, modernise later... Redesigning or rewriting the application [is a non-goal]

note: An exemplary migration plan: technically precise on the mechanisms it depends on, honest about the zero-downtime limit, risk-driven with early spikes and rehearsed fail-back, and free of all five traps.
